nodes.title: Quasicoherent derived sheaves
nodes.statement: For an ordinary qcqs scheme X define Dqc(X) as the full subcategory of D∞(O_X) on complexes with quasicoherent cohomology in every integer degree. Perf(X) is its full subcategory of objects locally represented by bounded complexes of finite projective modules. For X=Spec R the usual affine sheafification/global-sections comparison identifies Dqc(X) with D∞(R), including unbounded complexes.
proofSteps: Use the ordinary scheme/module sheaf definition of quasicoherence. Define the full enhanced subcategory and verify that the affine unbounded derived equivalence extends the module equivalence, using affine acyclicity and truncation convergence. Ordinary affine geometry inputs are recorded as a gap where the current baseline lacks the required API.
acceptance: O_SpecR corresponds to R[0].
The zero complex is quasicoherent and perfect.
On Spec ℤ, ⊕_{n∈ℕ}ℤ[0] is quasicoherent but is not perfect.

sources.match: Dqc is the quasicoherent full derived subcategory and uses ordinary scheme cohomology, not an animated replacement of X.

nodes.title: Derived base change on perfect schemes
nodes.statement: For a cartesian square X′→X over Y′→Y of perfect qcqs F_p-schemes, Lg*Rf*K→Rf′*Lg′*K is an equivalence for every K∈Dqc(X), without a flatness assumption on g or a boundedness assumption on K.
proofSteps: For X=Spec A, Y=Spec B, Y′=Spec B′, the required identity is A⊗ᴸ_B B′≃A′. Derive it from perfect-ring Tor independence. Cover the qcqs schemes by finitely many affines and use Čech descent and the finite cohomological bounds to transport the identity to unbounded quasicoherent complexes.
acceptance: The ring identity has base B: reversing the A and B factors would be ill-typed.
The analogous ordinary square over ℤ with both sides ℤ/p is not Tor independent.

sources.match: Perfect Tor independence supplies the affine change-of-rings identity; finite affine descent handles qcqs schemes.

nodes.title: The cohomology base-change map
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring map A→B and K∈D≥0(A), the canonical map H⁰(K)[0]→K induces H⁰(K)⊗_A B→H⁰(K⊗ᴸ_A B). It is functorial in K and in B, and compatible with successive scalar extensions. Flat B makes it an isomorphism; without flatness it can fail.
proofSteps: Identify H⁰(K)[0] with τ≤0K using K∈D≥0. Tensor the canonical truncation map and apply H⁰. Identify H⁰ of the degree-zero module tensor with the ordinary tensor. Naturality gives identity/composition; flatness follows from exact tensor.
acceptance: For A→A the comparison is identity.
For K=M[0], the degree-zero comparison is the usual isomorphism M⊗B≅H⁰(M⊗ᴸB).
For A=ℤ, B=ℤ/p and K=(ℤ/p)[−1] with H¹=ℤ/p, its source is zero and its target H⁰ is ℤ/p.

sources.locator: Lemma 5.3 and proof of Theorem 5.4, pp. 9–10

nodes.title: Splitting obstructions in a distinguished triangle
nodes.statement: For a distinguished triangle A→B→Q --δ→ A[1] in the chosen derived category, a map s:M→Q lifts to M→B if and only if δ∘s=0. In particular B→Q has a right inverse if and only if δ=0. An exact comparison functor carries this obstruction to the corresponding obstruction in the comparison triangle; vanishing after comparison implies vanishing before comparison only when the induced map on the relevant Hom group is injective.
proofSteps: Apply Hom(M,−) to the triangle and use exactness at Hom(M,Q). Specialize to s=id_Q. Transport the triangle by an exact functor and use its Hom comparison, keeping the injectivity condition explicit.
acceptance: For the split triangle A→A⊕Q→Q the connecting map is zero.
For 0→ℤ --p→ℤ→ℤ/p→0 the associated triangle does not split for p prime.
A nonconservative comparison functor cannot by itself certify an original splitting.

sources.match: The derived splitting class is killed through a comparison only after checking its detecting map.

nodes.title: Cofinality of the terminal fibre
nodes.statement: If p:E→B is coCartesian and b is terminal in B, inclusion E_b→E is final. More generally E_b→E×_B B_{/b} is final. Therefore the colimit of a diagram on the latter total category can be computed on E_b, whenever either colimit exists.
hypotheses: B is a quasicategory; the coCartesian total categories are therefore quasicategories as well.
proofSteps: For x over u transport x along u→b. This gives an initial object of the comma category x/E_b up to contractible choice. Apply the quasicategorical Theorem A finality criterion. Replace B by B/b for the general version.
acceptance: For an interval diagram C→D the terminal fibre D computes colimits over its Grothendieck total category.
The initial fibre C is not in general final.

sources.match: The finality criterion applies because coCartesian transport makes each comma category contractible.

nodes.title: The fibrewise edge-preservation criterion
nodes.statement: For coCartesian fibrations E,E′ over B and a functor F:E→E′ over B, F preserves coCartesian edges if and only if for every a:b→c and x∈E_b the canonical comparison a′_!F_b(x)→F_c(a_!x) is an equivalence. Such a functor corresponds under straightening to a coherent natural transformation of the classified diagrams.
hypotheses: B is a quasicategory; the coCartesian total categories are therefore quasicategories as well.
proofSteps: Factor the image of a coCartesian lift through a chosen lift in E′. The image is coCartesian exactly when the remaining vertical edge is an equivalence. Independence of choices follows from contractibility of lift spaces; straightening retains the naturality coherences.
acceptance: For a constant product fibration, an arbitrary fibre functor preserves transport edges exactly when its transport comparisons are equivalences.
A fibrewise functor together with noninvertible transport comparisons does not pass the criterion.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.4.4.3, PDF p. 149; §2.4.5 and Theorem 3.2.0.1, PDF pp. 150–155 and 187
sources.match: Factor an edge through a chosen coCartesian lift and compare its vertical residual equivalence.

nodes.title: Point-free coefficient-system comparison
nodes.statement: For a Grothendieck topos X presented by a fixed small site, in a larger ambient universe, and a sequence of sheaves of commutative rings R_n, the Cartesian full subcategory of the enhancement of R_•-module sheaves on Fun(ℕᵒᵖ,X) identifies, on mapping spaces as well as objects, with lim_n D∞(X,R_n) along derived scalar extension. This statement imposes no enough-points assumption; its localization proof is a separately recorded gap rather than an inference from the enough-points theorem.
proofSteps: Use the point-free injective model for ringed diagram sheaves and localize the derived transition maps. Identify its homotopy-coherent Cartesian sections by mapping-space localization. Prove both fully faithful mapping-space comparison and essential surjectivity of systems; the constant-diagram theorem alone does not prove the variable-coefficient case.
acceptance: For constant rings this is the constant diagram localization comparison.
For the coefficient tower R/I^n all transition tensors are derived.
An equivalence of triangulated homotopy categories is insufficient.

sources.match: Combinatorial model localization compares coherent and strict diagram categories.
The ordinary ringed-system description motivates the enhanced variable-coefficient comparison.

nodes.title: Space-valued representability
nodes.statement: If C is presentable, a functor F:Cᵒᵖ→Spaces is representable exactly when it preserves small limits. The space of representing objects with the representing equivalence is contractible. Presentable categories consequently admit small limits.
proofSteps: Express C as an accessible localization of a presheaf category. A limit-preserving space-valued functor extends to a representable presheaf functor; the local condition puts the representing object in C. Fully faithful Yoneda gives contractible uniqueness.
acceptance: For Map_C(−,c) the representing object is c.
The theorem is about space-valued functors, including all higher mapping homotopy groups.

sources.match: The presentable Yoneda argument produces representing objects and hence adjoints.

nodes.title: Accessible localization and coreflection
nodes.statement: Let C be presentable and S a small set of morphisms. An S-local object x is one for which Map(v,x)→Map(u,x) is an equivalence for every s:u→v in S. The full local subcategory C_S is presentable and its inclusion has an accessible left adjoint L_S. Separately, an accessible full presentable subcategory A⊂C closed under small colimits has a right adjoint G to its inclusion. These two adjoint directions are stated distinctly.
proofSteps: Run the accessible localization construction for the set S, or the equivalent presentable solution-set argument. Identify local objects by mapping-space orthogonality and the idempotent unit. For coreflection apply the right-adjoint theorem to the inclusion and identify its fully faithful counit.
acceptance: For S=∅, C_S=C and L_S is identity.
In a stable C, localizing at all generator maps g→0 gives the zero category when the generators detect zero objects.
For a colimit-closed presentable A, Map_C(i a,c)≃Map_A(a,Gc); exchanging the two Hom variables gives the wrong direction.

sources.locator: Proposition 5.5.4.15, PDF pp. 500–501; Corollary 5.5.2.9, PDF p. 484
sources.match: Localization at a small set is reflective; the colimit-preserving inclusion criterion gives coreflection.

nodes.title: Limits of presentable categories
nodes.statement: A homotopy pullback of presentable categories along left-adjoint functors is presentable, its projection functors are left adjoints, and its colimits are evaluated componentwise. More generally Prᴸ admits all small limits, and the forgetful functor Prᴸ→Cat∞ preserves them. Thus a coherent inverse limit of D∞(X,R/I^n) along scalar-change left adjoints is presentable.
proofSteps: For a pullback, lift objects together with an equivalence of their images; use a sufficiently large common accessibility cardinal to prove accessibility, and compute colimits componentwise. Products and homotopy pullbacks give all small limits. The coCartesian-sections comparison identifies the underlying coherent category.
acceptance: The product of a small family of presentable categories is presentable.
A limit of ordinary homotopy categories does not supply this result.
Inclusion of the completed sheaf category into the ambient category can fail colimit preservation although the category itself is presentable.

sources.match: The pullback theorem and arbitrary-limit theorem are needed together, with componentwise colimits.

nodes.title: Exactness and coproduct preservation
nodes.statement: An exact functor between stable quasicategories admitting small coproducts preserves all small colimits if and only if it preserves small coproducts. These stable categories admit all small colimits.
proofSteps: Express sequential colimits by the cofiber of 1−shift on a coproduct. Express a general colimit as the geometric realization of its simplicial replacement, and each realization as the sequential colimit of finite skeleta. Exactness handles finite skeleta and cofibres; coproduct preservation handles the remaining sums.
acceptance: Derived scalar extension is exact and coproduct-preserving, hence colimit-preserving.
An exact right adjoint need not preserve coproducts.

sources.match: Finite exactness together with coproduct preservation controls arbitrary colimits in stable categories.

nodes.title: The compact-generation adjoint criterion
nodes.statement: Let F:C⇄D:G be an adjunction of stable categories, with C compactly generated by a small set of compact objects and both categories admitting coproducts. If F sends the compact generators to compact objects, G preserves coproducts. Conversely, if G preserves coproducts, F sends every compact object to a compact object.
hypotheses: Compact generators detect equivalences by mapping from all their integer shifts. The left adjoint is exact, so their shifted images are compact as well.
proofSteps: For every integer shift of each compact generator c compare Map_C(c,⊕Gy_i) with Map_D(Fc,⊕y_i) using adjunction and compactness. The comparison is an equivalence on mapping spaces, so generator detection proves ⊕Gy_i→G(⊕y_i) is an equivalence. For the converse use the same adjunction for any compact c and arbitrary coproducts.
acceptance: For finite free R→S scalar extension, the restriction right adjoint preserves coproducts.
Compact generation of C is the detecting hypothesis; presentability alone does not replace it.

sources.locator: Proposition 1.4.4.1(3) and proof, p. 154; compact-generator detection in §1.4.4, pp. 155–156
sources.match: Mapping out of compact generators detects the coproduct comparison; this is the stable enhanced form of the Neeman criterion.
The geometric application uses preservation of compact objects to control a right adjoint.

nodes.title: Adjoints at cardinal cutoffs
nodes.statement: Suppose a filtered system of presentable categories D_κ has fully faithful transition functors, a fixed presentable C, and compatible colimit-preserving functors i_κ:C→D_κ. Let G_κ be the constructed right adjoints. Then G_λ restricted along D_κ→D_λ is naturally equivalent to G_κ, with all three-cutoff coherences. They assemble on the category of objects belonging to some adequate cutoff. If the source also varies as C_κ, additionally require that G_λ sends D_κ into the essential image of C_κ; compatibility is not automatic without this condition.
proofSteps: For y∈D_κ, adjunction and full faithfulness show that G_κy and G_λy represent the same functor on C. Yoneda produces the comparison, and its contractible uniqueness gives identity, composition and triple-cutoff coherence. Check the image condition separately when both source and target vary.
acceptance: The fixed-source étale coreflection setup has compatible right adjoints.
A larger ambient site does not by itself prove that a varying-source right adjoint has a small value.

sources.match: The étale subcategory is fixed while the ambient v-site cutoff grows; uniqueness then gives compatible right adjoints.

nodes.title: Coherent inverse towers and the product–difference formula
nodes.statement: For a stable enhanced category with countable products and a coherent inverse tower K:N(ℕᵒᵖ)→C, construct its homotopy limit as fib(1−s:∏_n K_n→∏_n K_n), where the nth component of s is the transition K_(n+1)→K_n after projection. This construction includes the projection cone and its mapping-space universal property. A strict tower of complexes or modules maps to a coherent tower by localization; an arbitrary ordinary diagram in hC is not silently substituted for it.
proofSteps: Construct the shift map from the coherent tower transitions. Its fibre carries compatible projections. Apply mapping spaces from any test object; the homotopy equalizer of product and shifted product is the inverse limit of the mapping-space tower. This proves the cone universal property and functoriality.
acceptance: The constant identity-transition tower has Rlim≃K.
If every transition is zero, 1−s is identity and Rlim=0.
The tower ℤ --×p←ℤ --×p←⋯ has lim=0 but lim¹=ℤ_p/ℤ for p prime, so its derived limit is nonzero in degree 1.

sources.locator: Derived Categories, Definition 13.34.1 (08TC), Lemma 13.34.2 (07KC), Remark 13.34.4 (0H9J), PDF pp. 105–106; Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.23.1 (0941), PDF pp. 47–48
sources.match: The product–difference triangle computes derived sequential inverse limits.
Ordinary module towers are used through their derived inverse limits.

nodes.title: Milnor exact sequence
nodes.statement: For a coherent tower K_n in D∞(O) on a replete topos, every integer q has a natural exact sequence 0→lim¹_n H^(q−1)(K_n)→H^q(Rlim_n K_n)→lim_n H^q(K_n)→0. Here lim¹ for a module-sheaf tower is the cokernel of its product–difference map. On an arbitrary topos use derived products instead; the simple sequence requires countable product exactness.
proofSteps: Exact countable products imply that cohomology of the product is the product of cohomology in every degree. The long exact sequence of the fibre triangle then separates into kernel and cokernel of 1−s. Identify those as lim and lim¹.
acceptance: For an eventually constant cohomology tower, the lim¹ term vanishes.
The statement covers negative and positive q alike.
For strict module towers in the point topos this is the ordinary module Milnor sequence.

sources.locator: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 21.23.2 (0D6K), PDF p. 48; use exact countable products for the sheaf-cohomology version
sources.match: The long exact sequence of the product–difference triangle yields Milnor when products are exact.

nodes.title: Ordinary pro-zero towers and pro-isomorphisms
nodes.statement: An ordinary module-sheaf tower M is pro-zero when for every n there is m≥n such that the transition M_m→M_n is zero. A morphism of ordinary module towers is a pro-isomorphism when its kernel and cokernel towers are pro-zero. For a morphism of coherent derived towers the required degreewise condition is that every cohomology tower of its cone is pro-zero; a uniform vanishing stage across all degrees is a stronger condition and is not part of this definition.
proofSteps: Use actual transition maps, not merely vanishing inverse limits. Form kernel, cokernel and cohomology towers functorially. Prove stability under cofinal reindexing and short exact sequences of ordinary towers.
acceptance: The zero tower is pro-zero.
An arbitrary nonzero family with zero transition maps is pro-zero.
For the tower ℤ with ×p transitions no transition into a fixed stage is zero; the tower is not pro-zero although lim is zero.

sources.locator: Definition 3.2, Lemmas 3.4–3.6 and Lemma 5.3, pp. 5–6 and 9

nodes.title: Derived inverse-limit invariance under pro-zero errors
nodes.statement: In a replete topos, a pro-zero ordinary module-sheaf tower has lim=lim¹=0. Hence a coherent derived tower whose every cohomology tower is pro-zero has Rlim=0. A morphism whose cone has this degreewise property induces an equivalence on Rlim. The strict pro-Tor error of unbounded coefficient systems must separately be shown degreewise pro-zero by the uniform finite-amplitude algebraic argument from DD.1.
proofSteps: For a pro-zero tower, solve (1−s)x=y by a finite sum in each component, since only finitely many composites into that fixed component are nonzero. Its kernel is zero; this proves both lim and lim¹ vanish. Apply Milnor in every integer degree to the cohomology towers of the cone, then use cohomology detection.
acceptance: The chosen killing stage may depend on n and on the cohomology degree.
Do not infer invariance after tensoring a variable unbounded tower solely from a degreewise pro-isomorphism of coefficient rings.

sources.match: The ordinary pro-zero specialization kills the derived inverse-limit error.
The unbounded pro-Tor application needs finite regular-sequence amplitude, not arbitrary tensor preservation of pro-zero systems.

nodes.title: Independence under hypercover refinement
nodes.statement: For a refinement V_•→U_• of hypercovers of X in a replete topos, pullback gives an equivalence D_cart(U_•)→D_cart(V_•), coherently compatible with refinement composition. Under either descent equivalence it identifies with id_{D∞(X)}. On the uniformly bounded-below Cartesian subcategories the same holds on an arbitrary topos.
proofSteps: Compose refinement pullback with augmentation pullback from D∞(X). The canonical comparison with the second augmentation is an equivalence. Apply the descent equivalences to deduce refinement equivalence; contractible inverse choices yield composition coherence.
acceptance: The identity refinement acts by identity.
Two successive refinements give the same functor as their composite up to the prescribed natural equivalence.
Refinement independence is stated for coherent Cartesian systems, not arbitrary simplicial derived objects.

sources.match: The descent equivalence identifies all refinements with the same original complex.

sources.locator: Simplicial Spaces, Lemmas 85.18.4 (0DA2) and 85.20.4 (0DA7), PDF pp. 43–45
sources.match: The bounded-below Cartesian equivalence is natural in the augmented hypercover.

nodes.title: Space-valued sheaves and Postnikov convergence
nodes.statement: For a small site, use the quasicategory of presheaves of Kan spaces and its accessible localization at covering descent maps to construct sheaves of spaces; localizing further at all hypercovers gives the hypercomplete subcategory. Form τ≤n and the coherent Postnikov tower there. Hypercompleteness means descent along all hypercovers; Postnikov completeness is the stronger convergence/effectivity assertion used here and is not automatic for every hypercomplete topos.
proofSteps: Construct space-valued presheaves using the coherent functor category and the Kan mapping-space model. Impose covering descent by accessible localization. Build truncation from n-truncated mapping targets and assemble its tower. Use exact weakly contractible sections or finite homotopy dimension for convergence; record the size of the hypercover localization and the effective-tower proof as explicit higher-sheaf inputs.
acceptance: On the point site, sheaves are spaces and every Postnikov tower converges.
A zero-truncated sheaf of spaces is the nerve of an ordinary sheaf of sets.
For n≥1, τ≤(n−1)K(ℤ,n) is a point while τ≤nK(ℤ,n)≃K(ℤ,n).

sources.locator: Definitions 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.2.6, Proposition 6.2.2.7 and Construction 6.2.2.9, PDF pp. 595–599; Proposition 6.5.2.8 and the hypercompletion construction, PDF pp. 686–687; Theorem 6.5.3.12 and Corollary 6.5.3.13, PDF p. 698; Definition 5.5.6.23 and Proposition 5.5.6.26, PDF pp. 516–517; Proposition 7.2.1.10 and proof, PDF pp. 738–739
sources.match: Sheaf and hypercomplete localizations are distinct; local finite homotopy dimension ensures convergent Postnikov towers.
Weakly contractible objects give exact sections and Postnikov convergence.

nodes.title: The h-topology on perfect schemes

nodes.title: h-descent for quasicoherent and perfect complexes
nodes.statement: The functor X↦Dqc(X) on perfect qcqs F_p-schemes satisfies h-Čech descent. Perf(X) satisfies h-hyperdescent. For perfectly finitely presented maps the bounded subcategory Dqcᵇ is functorial and satisfies h-descent, because finite Tor dimension preserves boundedness and h-covers detect boundedness. These statements do not assert unbounded h-hyperdescent over arbitrary perfect bases.
proofSteps: Use the preceding E2 geometric theorem that O_Y→Rf_*O_X is quantitatively descendable for an h-cover of perfect schemes (Witt Theorem 11.27, p. 46). Its proof needs fppf and proper Noetherian descendability, base-change control of the index, and a uniform bound along the countable Frobenius telescope (11.22–11.25, pp. 44–45); ordinary h-cover cohomology alone does not imply it. Apply the separately requested acyclic E5 abstract module-descent theorem to obtain Čech effectivity. Restrict to finite perfect amplitude for hyperdescent: the corresponding spaces are truncated, and a Cartesian hypercover datum retains the amplitude of its degree-zero member. Finite Tor dimension and h-boundedness detection handle Dqcᵇ.
acceptance: Perfect complexes carry a uniform local finite amplitude along the hypercover.
Do not replace an h-Čech theorem for unbounded Dqc by a hyperdescent theorem without the finite-dimensional base condition.

sources.locator: Theorem 11.2(1)–(3), p. 40; Lemmas 11.22–11.23 and Proposition 11.25, pp. 44–45; Theorem 11.27 and proof, p. 46; amplitude argument, pp. 46–48
sources.match: Categorical h-descent, finite perfect-amplitude descent and boundedness detection have distinct hypotheses.

nodes.title: Boundedness detected by perfect h-covers
nodes.statement: For an h-cover f:X→Y of perfect qcqs schemes and K∈Dqc(Y), if Lf*K is bounded, K is bounded. On perfectly finitely presented schemes finite Tor dimension also proves that pullback preserves bounded complexes.
proofSteps: For the perfection of an fppf cover use faithful-flat detection on cohomology. For proper covers refine to modifications and induct on the closed complement. The proper-modification pullback square for structure sheaves, projection formula and finite cohomological dimension identify K as a finite pullback of bounded complexes. The scheme-theoretic refinement theorem is an ordinary-geometry proof input recorded in gaps.
acceptance: The theorem detects a two-sided bound of K; it does not say arbitrary ring maps reflect boundedness.
The finite-presentation condition is kept in the separate preservation statement.

sources.locator: Lemma 11.30 and proof of Theorem 11.2(3), pp. 47–48
sources.match: Refine into fppf and proper modifications and induct on the modification level.

nodes.title: Tensor and bounded cosimplicial totalization
nodes.statement: If R has finite global dimension, N• is a cosimplicial ordinary R-module (each term in degree zero), and Tot N• is bounded, then for any unbounded M∈D∞(R) the canonical map M⊗ᴸ_R Tot N•→Tot(M⊗ᴸ_R N•) is an equivalence. It does not assert that arbitrary tensor products preserve arbitrary totalizations of unbounded cosimplicial complexes.
proofSteps: Use the common global-dimension bound to compare tensor of unbounded M with its cochain truncations against bounded complexes. For bounded M reduce to projective modules; Dold–Kan computes the totalization. Then use uniform cohomological bounds on Tot N• and on degree-zero N^n to pass through truncation towers degree by degree.
acceptance: For a constant cosimplicial module N this is the identity comparison.
The boundedness of Tot N• and the degree-zero condition on N^n are both retained.

sources.match: Finite global dimension gives uniform Tor bounds and allows the two truncation/totalization limits to commute.

nodes.title: Unbounded h-hyperdescent over a finite-dimensional perfect base
nodes.statement: Let k be the perfection of a regular Noetherian F_p-algebra of finite Krull dimension. On perfectly finitely presented perfect k-schemes, X↦Dqc(X) satisfies h-hyperdescent. For an h-hypercover X•→Y and any K∈Dqc(Y), RΓ(Y,K)≃Tot RΓ(X•,K|X•); every coherent Cartesian Dqc datum is effective.
proofSteps: Refine to an affine hypercover. The structure-sheaf totalization is the degree-zero base ring; finite global dimension and the tensor-totalization theorem give RΓ hyperdescent for any K. For a Cartesian datum define its hypercomplete sheaf by totalization after every base change; it restricts to the prescribed terms. Restrict to X⁰ and use already-proved h-Čech effectivity to obtain a quasicoherent object on Y.
acceptance: The bound is on the ordinary regular presentation of the perfect base; it is not an assertion for every perfect ring.
The conclusion is an enhanced categorical equivalence, including mapping spaces and essential surjectivity.

sources.locator: Theorem 11.2(4), p. 40; Lemmas 11.37–11.38 and Remark 11.39, pp. 50–51
sources.match: Mapping hyperdescent follows from bounded totalization; Čech effectivity supplies object effectivity.

nodes.title: Full enhanced subcategories
nodes.statement: Given a vertex predicate P on C, take exactly those simplices all of whose vertices satisfy P. The inclusion is full; when C is a quasicategory so is this simplicial subset. Its vertices identify with the subtype of vertices satisfying P.
hypotheses: Fix a small universe u and the next universe u+1; categorical assertions assume quasicategories.
proofSteps: Select simplices by their vertex restrictions; faces and degeneracies preserve this condition.
Inner horns whose vertices satisfy P can be filled in C, and every vertex of the filler already occurs in the horn. Use the ordinary nerve comparison to check fullness.
acceptance: Taking P true gives C.
Taking P false gives the empty simplicial set.
For N(A), restricting the vertices to P gives the nerve of the pinned ordinary full subcategory.

nodes.title: Maximal Kan core
nodes.statement: For a quasicategory C, its core is the simplicial subset containing precisely the simplices whose edges are equivalences. It has every vertex of C and is Kan. Every map from a Kan complex into C factors uniquely through it.
hypotheses: Fix a small universe u and the next universe u+1; categorical assertions assume quasicategories.
proofSteps: The subset is a quasicategory by inner horn filling. An inverse of a retained edge is itself an equivalence, so remains in the subset.
The equivalence-edge outer horn criterion makes the subset Kan; maps from Kan complexes preserve equivalences and therefore factor.
acceptance: The core of Δ[0] is Δ[0].
The core of Δ[1] is the discrete two-point space.
A Kan complex is equal to its own core up to simplicial isomorphism.

nodes.title: The infinity category of small categories
nodes.statement: Build Cat∞ from the simplicial category whose objects are u-small quasicategories and whose enriched maps from C to D are the core of Fun(C,D). Its homotopy-coherent nerve is a quasicategory in u+1. Thus Map_Cat∞(C,D) is equivalent to core Fun(C,D), retaining functors and invertible transformations of every order.
hypotheses: Fix a small universe u and the next universe u+1; categorical assertions assume quasicategories.
proofSteps: Use strictly associative internal-Hom composition restricted to cores. Its mapping objects are Kan by the core theorem.
The homotopy-coherent nerve of this locally Kan simplicial category is a quasicategory; compare its right mapping spaces with the enriched mapping objects. Track the u to u+1 lift explicitly.
acceptance: Mapping any C to the terminal category gives a contractible space.
Maps out of Δ[1] retain the core of the coherent arrow category.
Map_Cat∞(Δ[0],Δ[1]) has two components, so is not contractible. Replacing the core by the whole interval would give the wrong space.

Apply the locally Kan coherent-nerve theorem and its mapping-space comparison; the terminal, empty and finite discrete calculations test the carrier.

nodes.title: Universe control for mapping spaces
nodes.statement: For a quasicategory C in u+1, local u-smallness means that every right mapping Kan complex is homotopy equivalent to a u-small Kan complex after universe lift. Choose such small models and comparison equivalences. The coherent representable Map_C(x,−) lands in Spaces_u, with evaluation naturally equivalent to the chosen model at y. The underlying simplex type of the original mapping space need not itself be u-small.
hypotheses: Fix a small universe u and the next universe u+1; categorical assertions assume quasicategories.
proofSteps: Use essential smallness of mapping spaces, equivalently a small Kan model with homotopy-inverse comparison maps. HTT 5.4.1.5 explains the homotopy-group/minimal-model criterion; 5.4.1.7 is the local-smallness definition.

Transport the coherent mapping functor through the full inclusion Spaces_u into larger spaces. Existence of small models at every vertex puts its essential image there; transfer the diagram with all coherence, rather than choosing unrelated vertexwise assignments.
Compare evaluation by natural equivalences. A contractible large Kan model is the regression case distinguishing homotopy size from raw simplex size.
acceptance: The lift of a u-small simplicial set is locally u-small.
The category of u-small sets is locally u-small.
The nerve of an ordinary category with a Hom type that is not u-small fails local u-smallness.

sources.locator: Corollary 5.4.1.5 and Proposition 5.4.1.7, printed pp. 421–423 (PDF pp. 439–441)
sources.match: Local smallness concerns the homotopy type of each mapping space; a small Kan model, not raw simplex smallness, is required.

nodes.title: Cardinal filteredness of coherent diagrams
nodes.statement: For an infinite regular cardinal κ and a quasicategory K, require every map Y→K with fewer than κ nondegenerate simplices to extend to Y⋆Δ[0]→K. This is κ-filteredness. The empty Y requires a vertex in K; the finite discrete two-point diagram requires a common cocone.
hypotheses: Fix a small universe u and the next universe u+1; categorical assertions assume quasicategories.
proofSteps: Use the join from E0 and count nondegenerate simplices, not all degenerate simplices.
For ordinary posets recover upper bounds of fewer than κ vertices; compare the finite-cone definition and the higher horn coherences.
acceptance: Δ[0] is κ-filtered for every infinite regular κ.
The empty simplicial set is not κ-filtered.
The nerve of the discrete two-point category is not ω-filtered.

nodes.title: Coherent nerve of a locally Kan category
nodes.statement: For a simplicial category C whose enriched mapping objects are Kan complexes, its homotopy-coherent nerve N(C) is a quasicategory. For objects x,y, its right mapping space is naturally equivalent to the enriched mapping Kan complex C(x,y). The comparison retains composition in the homotopy category and is natural in simplicial functors.
hypotheses: Fix object and mapping universes and raise mapping objects to the universe of the coherent nerve when necessary.
All enriched mapping objects are Kan; ordinary simplicial categories without this hypothesis are not covered.
proofSteps: Translate an inner-horn extension into extension along the corresponding simplicial thickening. Only the endpoint mapping cube differs; its punctured-cube inclusion is anodyne, so the Kan hypothesis gives a filler (HTT 1.1.5.10).

Identify the right mapping space with Sing_Q C(x,y) using HTT 2.2.2.13. The Q realization/singular Quillen equivalence and its natural comparison for Kan objects identify this with C(x,y) (2.2.2.7–11).
Check enriched composition on the resulting homotopy mapping spaces and track universe lifts. This is a general theorem, independently of the DG nerve comparison.
acceptance: The nerve is a quasicategory and its mapping comparison is a space equivalence, without assuming either conclusion as an input field.
For a discrete ordinary category the comparison recovers its Hom sets; for a one-object simplicial group it retains the full mapping group.

sources.locator: Proposition 1.1.5.10 and proof, printed pp. 23–24 (PDF pp. 41–42); Propositions 2.2.2.7, 2.2.2.9, 2.2.2.13 and Remark 2.2.2.11, printed pp. 76–78 (PDF pp. 94–96)
sources.match: The locally Kan hypothesis supplies horn fillers, and the Q-singular description compares right mapping spaces with enriched Hom.

nodes.title: Koszul complexes
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring A, an A-module E and a linear map φ:E→A, construct a cochain complex K_A(φ) with K^(−q)=∧^q_A E for q≥0 and zero terms in positive degrees. On a decomposable wedge the differential deletes e_j with coefficient (−1)^(j−1)φ(e_j). Exterior multiplication makes this a differential graded A-algebra. For f=(f₁,…,fᵣ), specialize to E=A^r and φ(e_i)=f_i; this complex occupies [−r,0] and augments to A/(f). Arbitrary E is allowed; bounded perfectness is asserted for finite projective E.
hypotheses: A is commutative; cohomological grading and the E1 tensor signs are fixed.
For a finite regular sequence the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. No regularity is required to define the complex.
proofSteps: Descend alternating contraction through the existing exterior-power universal property, including the repeated-vector relation in characteristic two. The two terms deleting any given pair cancel, proving d²=0.
Check the graded Leibniz rule and functoriality for ψ:E→E′ with φ′ψ=φ on decomposable wedges, then use their spanning property.
For finite sequences identify the exterior decomposition with the signed tensor of the one-element complexes. Induction by the cone of multiplication proves the regular-sequence resolution.
acceptance: For one element the differential is multiplication by that element, rather than zero.
The zero one-element sequence has nonzero H^(−1), so replacing a Koszul complex by its ordinary quotient fails this test.

sources.match: Exterior contraction defines the differential and its functoriality; a regular sequence resolves the quotient.

nodes.title: Koszul power model for completion
nodes.statement: For a finite ideal I=(f₁,…,fᵣ) in a commutative ring A and any unbounded K∈D∞(A), the E4 completion reflector has the natural model L_I K≃Rlim_n(K⊗ᴸ_A K_A(f₁^n,…,fᵣ^n)), n≥1. The transition from m to n (m≥n) is identity in degree zero and sends the i-th exterior generator to f_i^(m−n)e_i. No Noetherian or regular-sequence hypothesis is imposed; these are Koszul reductions, not ordinary quotient rings.
hypotheses: Use the enhanced coherent inverse limit, the E1 signed tensor and E4 reflector specialized to the point topos.
The same finite construction over a ringed slice is compatible with restriction; its enhanced comparison uses the recorded point-free localization interface.
proofSteps: The transition formula follows from Koszul functoriality and preserves augmentations. Each f_i^n acts null-homotopically, so every tensor term and its limit are complete.

Filter each Koszul complex by degree. For a complete K the inverse limit of every negative graded piece is a finite sum of scalar telescopes for products of the generators; radical-ideal closure makes these vanish. The unit is therefore an equivalence on complete objects.

Compare the inverse-limit functor with the reflector using the dual finite-free Koszul model of the extended Čech localization complex. Tensor–Hom adjunction gives the natural mapping-space universal property and hence identifies the reflector.
acceptance: The empty ideal tower is constant K and has completion K.
For I=(p) and K=Z[0], the ordinary quotient comparison applies; for arbitrary ideals only the Koszul model is asserted.

sources.locator: Situation 93.15 and Lemmas 93.16–93.18, pp. 266–267 (tags 0BKC, 091Y, 091Z, 0920); extended Čech comparison, Lemma 30.6, pp. 74–75 (0913)
sources.match: The correct inverse transition direction and finite duality identify the Koszul tower with the reflector for arbitrary complexes.

nodes.title: Regular ideal quotient algebra
nodes.statement: Let I=(f₁,…,fᵣ) be generated by a finite regular sequence in a commutative ring A. The ideals J_n=(f₁^n,…,fᵣ^n) are cofinal with I^n, K_A(f₁^n,…,fᵣ^n) resolves A/J_n, and gr_I A is the polynomial algebra over A/I on the generator classes. Every A/I^n is perfect over A with Tor-amplitude contained in [−r,0]. Thus for any unbounded K the Koszul completion model identifies naturally with Rlim_n(K⊗ᴸ_A A/I^n). These assertions do not require Noetherianity.
hypotheses: I is generated by a finite regular sequence; arbitrary finitely generated ideals are not covered by this ordinary quotient model.
proofSteps: Powers of a regular sequence remain Koszul-regular; use the E1 resolution. Compare J_n⊂I^n and I^(r(n−1)+1)⊂J_n to obtain cofinality.

Regular implies Koszul-regular, H₁-regular and quasi-regular; the last condition gives the polynomial associated graded. Each I^j/I^(j+1) is finite free over A/I, and a finite filtration gives perfect A/I^n with the same uniform Tor-amplitude bound.

Replace the Koszul terms by A/J_n and use cofinality in the enhanced limit. For sheaf coefficient applications these finite perfect calculations are used on every slice. The stronger varying-coefficient pro-Tor comparison is the separate E4 node, not a consequence of cofinality alone.
acceptance: For a principal non-zero-divisor f, K_A(f^n) resolves A/f^n.
For A=k[x,y] and I=(x,y), quotient powers have bounded perfect resolutions even though they are not the two-generator Koszul quotient J_n.
The sequence (0) in a nonzero ring fails the resolution claim and must retain its negative Koszul cohomology.

sources.match: Regularity and the quasi-regular associated graded control quotient powers and the finite amplitude.

sources.locator: Regular-ideal discussion after Lemma 3.5.4 and proof of 3.5.5, p. 25
sources.match: Finite regular-sequence algebra supplies the ordinary coefficient reduction argument.

sources.locator: Proof of Proposition 26.2 and Remark 26.3, p. 162
sources.match: The perfect regular-ideal quotients remove Noetherianity and support exact linear coefficient changes.

nodes.title: Quantitative descendability of perfect h-covers
nodes.statement: For an h-cover f:X→Y of perfect qcqs F_p-schemes, the structure-algebra map O_Y→Rf_*O_X is descendable: the canonical tensor power of its fibre maps null-homotopically to O_Y for some finite positive power. No uniform index over all h-covers is asserted. In the Frobenius approximation of a fixed fppf or proper Noetherian cover, the index is bounded independently of the approximation stage.
hypotheses: Use the E1 unbounded Dqc enhancement and coherent tensor/derived base change. Ordinary geometry and finite Noetherian cover bounds are the requested lower-tier D0 inputs.
proofSteps: Refine and approximate the cover by perfections of fppf or proper surjective maps of Noetherian schemes. Import the ordinary geometric tensor-nilpotence bound there, and lift its vanishing map through the E1 ordinary/enhanced comparison.

Base change along the Frobenius approximation preserves a fixed nilpotence exponent. The geometric Frobenius/Tor-vanishing bridge identifies the perfected limit of derived fibre products with the ordinary perfect fibre product; its formal comparison is an explicit geometry gap, rather than an assumed full animation theory.

For the countable telescope, the possible obstruction lies in lim¹ of mapping groups. Tensor two obstruction maps: their product lies in lim², which vanishes for a sequential tower. Thus a uniform exponent m gives an exponent at most 2m after passage to the limit. Use the E2 coherent Milnor calculation; abstract E5 module descent is not used to prove this geometric input.
acceptance: The index bound is uniform along the fixed Frobenius sequence, not merely finite separately at each stage.
An arbitrary filtered colimit of descendable maps is not inferred to be descendable; Witt Example 11.21 supplies the counterexample.

sources.locator: Lemma 11.22 and Lemma 11.23, p. 44; Proposition 11.25, p. 45; Theorem 11.27 and proof, p. 46; Frobenius comparison Proposition 11.6, pp. 41–42
sources.match: Noetherian geometric bounds survive Frobenius base change uniformly, and the countable telescope argument retains descendability.

sourceIssues.locator: Author copy SHA-256 99b418…14c7, Proposition 3.3.3, p. 19, essential-surjectivity paragraph and product display.
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts H^i(K) ≃ H^i(K_i) for every i ∈ N.
sourceIssues.correction: Treat each cohomological degree m∈ℤ. The tower H^m(K_n) stabilizes for n≥max(0,−m); apply the product-difference/Milnor calculation to its eventual constant tail. Do not identify the full product with the tail by dropping a finite prefix.
sourceIssues.reason: Checking only nonnegative i misses every negative cohomology group. The completion tower of A[1] has nonzero H^(−1). Moreover the displayed equality dropping factors with n<i is not justified: for the constant tower A[−1] and i=1 the omitted first H¹ factor is A, and the projection dropping it is not injective. The corrected argument uses eventual constancy separately in m and m−1 and proves the intended theorem.

To conclude that the category is left-complete, require the convergence condition for every complex, and verify reconstruction of compatible towers.

sourceIssues.correction: With X=Spec A, Y=Spec B, Y′=Spec B′ and X′=Spec A′, use A⊗ᴸ_B B′≃A′. Then K⊗ᴸ_A A′≃K⊗ᴸ_B B′ by derived tensor associativity.

sourceIssues.locator: Author copy SHA-256 99b418…14c7, Lemma 3.3.2, printed p. 18, the truncation comparison and final termwise RHom assertion. Visual page inspection on 2026-10-11.
sourceIssues.printed: The proof uses truncation adjunction to identify full derived Hom complexes termwise, both from K to L_n and from F_(n+1) to G_n.
sourceIssues.correction: Use mapping spaces (equivalently the nonpositive part of the mapping complex), take their coherent inverse limit, and deduce the intended derived-limit adjunction. Do not claim a termwise comparison of all integer degrees of RHom.
sourceIssues.reason: On the point topos take K=ℤ[1] and L_n=ℤ[0]. At n=0, τ≥0K=0 but RHom(K,L_0)=ℤ[−1] has H¹=ℤ. Likewise the compatible tower F_0=0, F_n=ℤ[1] for n≥1 and the constant compatible tower G_n=ℤ[0] give different H¹ for RHom(F_1,G_0) and RHom(F_0,G_0). Their mapping spaces are both contractible, as truncation adjunction actually requires. This corrects the proof and does not refute the adjunction theorem.
